// Helper functions: Sort the publication list by year
var sortedPublications = Object.values(publication_list).sort(function (a, b) {
  return b['year'] - a['year'];
}); // Sort descending by year

// Group publications by year
var groupedByYear = sortedPublications.reduce(function (acc, publication) {
  var year = publication.year;
  if (!acc[year]) {
    acc[year] = []; // Initialize an empty array for each year
  }
  acc[year].push(publication); // Push the publication into the respective year group
  return acc;
}, {});

// Main class

var PublicationList = function (_React$Component) {
  _inherits(PublicationList, _React$Component);

  function PublicationList(props) {
    _classCallCheck(this, PublicationList);

    return _possibleConstructorReturn(this, (PublicationList.__proto__ || Object.getPrototypeOf(PublicationList)).call(this, props));
  }

  _createClass(PublicationList, [{
    key: 'make_online_list',
    value: function make_online_list() {
      // manage the element to be displayed
      var list = [];

      var years = Object.keys(groupedByYear).sort(function (a, b) {
        return b - a;
      });
      // console.log(years);
      if (window.last_year_only) {
        years.length = 4; // Keep only the first item
        // console.log(years);
      }

      // for grouping the papers before a certain year
      var early_group_year = 2017;
      var early_year_met = false;

      years.forEach(function (year) {
        // Add a title for the year
        if (year > early_group_year) {
          list.push(React.createElement(
            'h2',
            { key: year, className: 'publication-year-title', id: year, 'data-aos': 'fade-up' },
            year
          ));
        } else {
          if (!early_year_met) {
            list.push(React.createElement(
              'h2',
              { key: year, className: 'publication-year-title', id: year, 'data-aos': 'fade-up' },
              early_group_year,
              ' and before'
            ));
            early_year_met = true;
          }
        }

        // Render the publications for that year
        groupedByYear[year].forEach(function (publication, index) {
          list.push(React.createElement(
            'div',
            { className: 'publication-row', id: index, key: publication.title, 'data-aos': 'fade-up', 'data-aos-delay': index * 20 },
            publication.image && React.createElement(
              'div',
              { className: 'publication-image' },
              React.createElement('img', { src: publication.image, alt: publication.title, loading: 'lazy' })
            ),
            React.createElement(
              'div',

                )
              ),

                publication.venue

              React.createElement(

                  'a',

                  'a',

                ),

}(React.Component);

ReactDOM.render(React.createElement(FeaturesSection, null), document.getElementById("features"));
//# sourceMappingURL=data:application/json;base64,</script></head>

      <div class="slideshow-container aos-init aos-animate" data-aos="fade-up"></div>
        <img src="/assets/img/photos/photo_all0.JPG" alt="" loading="lazy" style="display: none;">
        <img src="/assets/img/photos/photo_all1.jpeg" alt="" loading="lazy" style="display: none;">
        <img src="/assets/img/photos/HDSI 5-Year Celebration (151 of 425).jpg" alt="" loading="lazy" style="display: block;">
        <img src="/assets/img/photos/prof_and_bhanu.jpg" alt="" loading="lazy" style="display: none;">
        <img src="/assets/img/photos/HDSI 5-Year Celebration (162 of 425).jpg" alt="" loading="lazy" style="display: none;">
    
    
    <script>
          document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', () => {
          const container = document.querySelector("#home");
          const slides = container.querySelectorAll('img');
          // console.log(slides);
  
          if (slides.length === 0) {
              console.error('Image path error.');
              return;
          }
          // console.log(slides);
  
          let currentIndex = slides.length-1;
  
          function showNextSlide() {
            // console.log(currentIndex);
              // hide current image
              slides[currentIndex].style.display = 'none';
              // calculate next idx
              currentIndex = (currentIndex - 1);
              if (currentIndex < 0){
                currentIndex = slides.length-1;
              }
              // display next image
              slides[currentIndex].style.display = 'block';
              // console.log(currentIndex);
              // console.log(slides[currentIndex].style.display);
          }
  
          setInterval(showNextSlide, 5000);
        });
  </script>

      <div class="container">
        <div class="row">
          <div class="col-lg-10">
            <h2 data-aos="fade-up" data-aos-delay="100" class="aos-init aos-animate">Mobile Sensing and Ubiquitous Computing Laboratory</h2>
            <p data-aos="fade-up" data-aos-delay="200" class="aos-init aos-animate">We are a research team, led by Prof. Tauhidur Rahman, dedicated to designing next-generation AI-enabled mobile sensing systems to address real-world challenges.</p>

    <section id="about" class="about section light-background">

      <div class="container aos-init aos-animate" data-aos="fade-up" data-aos-delay="100">
        <div class="row align-items-xl-center gy-5">

          <div class="col-xl-5 content">
            <h3>About Us</h3>
            <h2>Mobile Sensing and Ubiquitous Computing Laboratory</h2>
            <!-- <p>We develop innovative health sensing technologies to translate physical signals into practical insights for better health understanding.</p> -->
            <p>
              The Mobile Sensing and Ubiquitous Computing Laboratory at the University of California San Diego conducts research on large-scale sensor data systems and multimodal AI/ML for health and behavior modeling. Our focus is on building scalable, energy-efficient sensor data systems through the use of heterogeneous sensor modalities and platforms for solving real-world problems.
            </p>
            <a href="#" class="read-more"><span>Read More</span><i class="bi bi-arrow-right"></i></a>
          </div>

          <div class="col-xl-7">
            <div class="row gy-4 icon-boxes">

              <div class="col-md-6 aos-init aos-animate" data-aos="fade-up" data-aos-delay="200">
                <div class="icon-box">
                  <i class="bi bi-buildings"></i>
                  <h3>Who we are</h3>
                  <p>We are a team of Mobile Sensing and AI-for-Health researchers led by Prof. Tauhidur Rahman, affiliated with UC San Diego's Halıcıoğlu Data Science Institute.</p>
                </div>
              </div> <!-- End Icon Box -->

              <div class="col-md-6 aos-init aos-animate" data-aos="fade-up" data-aos-delay="300">
                <div class="icon-box">
                  <i class="bi bi-clipboard-pulse"></i>
                  <h3>Research Interest</h3>
                <!-- <p>We explore novel health sensing technologies that transform acoustic and electromagnetic signals from the body and environment into actionable biological and behavioral insights.</p> -->
                <p>We leverage diverse sensor technologies to develop practical solutions, translating environmental and physiological signals into meaningful data that address real-world challenges.</p>
              </div>
              </div> <!-- End Icon Box -->

              <div class="col-md-6 aos-init aos-animate" data-aos="fade-up" data-aos-delay="400">
                <div class="icon-box">
                  <i class="bi bi-command"></i>
                  <h3>Lab Culture</h3>
                  <p>We foster a collaborative, inclusive, and innovation-driven lab culture that values curiosity and interdisciplinary thinking.</p>
                </div>
              </div> <!-- End Icon Box -->

              <div class="col-md-6 aos-init aos-animate" data-aos="fade-up" data-aos-delay="500">
                <div class="icon-box">
                  <i class="bi bi-graph-up-arrow"></i>
                  <h3>Our Vision</h3>
                  <p>We aim to advance ubiquitous and mobile health sensing to improve lives and revolutionize healthcare accessibility worldwide.</p>
                </div>
              </div> <!-- End Icon Box -->

            </div>

      <div class="container">
        <div class="container" id="project_list"><div class="row gy-4"><div class="col-xl-4 col-md-6 aos-init aos-animate" data-aos="fade-up" data-aos-delay="100"><article><div class="post-img"><a href="projects-details.html?project_name=mobile_health"><img src="assets/img/projects/mobile_health.png" alt="" class="img-fluid" loading="lazy"></a></div><p class="post-category">Wearable Devices | Smart Health Monitoring</p><h2 class="title"><a href="projects-details.html?project_name=mobile_health">Mobile Health Sensing</a></h2><div class="d-flex align-items-center"><div class="post-meta"><p class="post-author">Developing wearable and mobile systems to monitor health outcomes. Our work focuses on creating wearable devices that provide accurate, real-time health monitoring to support medical decisions.</p><p class="post-date">On going</p></div></div></article></div><div class="col-xl-4 col-md-6 aos-init aos-animate" data-aos="fade-up" data-aos-delay="100"><article><div class="post-img"><a href="projects-details.html?project_name=cog_health"><img src="assets/img/projects/cog_health.png" alt="" class="img-fluid" loading="lazy"></a></div><p class="post-category">Machine Learning | Applied AI</p><h2 class="title"><a href="projects-details.html?project_name=cog_health">Cognitive and Behavioral Health</a></h2><div class="d-flex align-items-center"><div class="post-meta"><p class="post-author">Exploring the interaction between cognitive processes and physiological signals. This theme aims to understand how behavior and brain activity influence mental health and cognitive performance.</p><p class="post-date">On going</p></div></div></article></div><div class="col-xl-4 col-md-6 aos-init aos-animate" data-aos="fade-up" data-aos-delay="100"><article><div class="post-img"><a href="projects-details.html?project_name=digital_epi"><img src="assets/img/projects/digital_epi.png" alt="" class="img-fluid" loading="lazy"></a></div><p class="post-category">Machine Learning | Contactless Sensing | Health Dataset</p><h2 class="title"><a href="projects-details.html?project_name=digital_epi">Digital Epidemiology</a></h2><div class="d-flex align-items-center"><div class="post-meta"><p class="post-author">Researching health trends and disease outbreaks using digital biomarkers. Projects in this theme address syndromic surveillance and health monitoring in public spaces.</p><p class="post-date">On going</p></div></div></article></div><div class="col-xl-4 col-md-6 aos-init aos-animate" data-aos="fade-up" data-aos-delay="100"><article><div class="post-img"><a href="projects-details.html?project_name=signal_ai"><img src="assets/img/projects/signal_ai.png" alt="" class="img-fluid" loading="lazy"></a></div><p class="post-category">Signal Processing | Deep Learning</p><h2 class="title"><a href="projects-details.html?project_name=signal_ai">Signal Processing and AI</a></h2><div class="d-flex align-items-center"><div class="post-meta"><p class="post-author">Leveraging AI and signal processing for ubiquitous computing challenges. This includes creating efficient algorithms to enhance image resolution and adapt models for diverse applications.</p><p class="post-date">On going</p></div></div></article></div><div class="col-xl-4 col-md-6 aos-init aos-animate" data-aos="fade-up" data-aos-delay="100"><article><div class="post-img"><a href="projects-details.html?project_name=interact_sys"><img src="assets/img/projects/interact_sys.png" alt="" class="img-fluid" loading="lazy"></a></div><p class="post-category">Sensors | HCI</p><h2 class="title"><a href="projects-details.html?project_name=interact_sys">Interaction Systems</a></h2><div class="d-flex align-items-center"><div class="post-meta"><p class="post-author">Designing human-centered systems that integrate seamlessly with daily life. <section id="features" class="features section"><section id="features" class="features section"><div class="container section-title aos-init aos-animate" data-aos="fade-up"><h2>Spotlight</h2><a href="https://www.youtube.com/@mosaiclab-ucsd/videos" target="_blank">Explore our groundbreaking research in action through featured videos</a></div><div class="container"><div class="row gy-4 align-items-center features-item aos-init aos-animate" data-aos="fade-up" data-aos-delay="0"><div class="col-lg-5 d-flex justify-content-center flex-column"><h3>YeLan: Neuromorphic High-Frequency 3D Dancing Pose Estimation in Dynamic Environment</h3><p>YeLan is an event camera-based 3D human pose estimation system designed for dynamic and low-light environments, outperforming conventional RGB and RGB-Depth solutions in robustness and energy efficiency.</p><ul><li><i class="bi bi-check"></i> <span>First event camera-based 3D dancing pose estimation system.</span></li><li><i class="bi bi-check"></i> <span>Operates effectively in low-light conditions and dynamic backgrounds.</span></li><li><i class="bi bi-check"></i> <span>Collected the world's first event camera dance dataset.</span></li><li><i class="bi bi-check"></i> <span>Developed a fully customizable motion-to-event physics-aware simulator.</span></li><li><i class="bi bi-check"></i> <span>Demonstrates robustness against clothing variations, background motion, occlusion, and lighting fluctuations.</span></li></ul><a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=xmqMgzqAxIM" class="btn btn-get-started align-self-start" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Learn More</a></div><div class="col-lg-7 d-flex align-items-center justify-content-center"><iframe width="100%" height="400" src="https://www.youtube.com/embed/xmqMgzqAxIM" title="YeLan: Neuromorphic High-Frequency 3D Dancing Pose Estimation in Dynamic Environment" frameborder="0" allow="accelerometer; autoplay; clipboard-write; encrypted-media; gyroscope; picture-in-picture" allowfullscreen="" style="border-radius: 10px; box-shadow: rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.1) 0px 4px 20px;"></iframe></div></div><div class="row gy-4 align-items-center features-item flex-row-reverse aos-init aos-animate" data-aos="fade-up" data-aos-delay="100"><div class="col-lg-5 d-flex justify-content-center flex-column"><h3>MechanoBeat: Monitoring Interactions with Everyday Objects using 3D Printed Harmonic Oscillators and Ultra-Wideband Radar</h3><p>MechanoBeat uses 3D printed mechanical tags and ultra-wideband radar to monitor interactions with objects, enabling battery-free, scalable, and unobtrusive sensing of both stationary and mobile objects.</p><ul><li><i class="bi bi-check"></i> <span>3D printed mechanical tags oscillate at unique frequencies upon interaction.</span></li><li><i class="bi bi-check"></i> <span>Monitors interactions without requiring batteries, silicon chips, or electronics.</span></li><li><i class="bi bi-check"></i> <span>Uses ultra-wideband (UWB) radar to locate and identify tag vibrations.</span></li><li><i class="bi bi-check"></i> <span>Capable of detecting simultaneous interactions with high accuracy, even in noisy environments.</span></li><li><i class="bi bi-check"></i> <span>Senses interactions behind walls using UWB radar in non-line-of-sight (NLOS) scenarios.</span></li></ul><a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ZXA_eKm_bR8" class="btn btn-get-started align-self-start" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Learn More</a></div><div class="col-lg-7 d-flex align-items-center justify-content-center"><iframe width="100%" height="400" src="https://www.youtube.com/embed/ZXA_eKm_bR8" title="MechanoBeat: Monitoring Interactions with Everyday Objects using 3D Printed Harmonic Oscillators and Ultra-Wideband Radar" frameborder="0" allow="accelerometer; autoplay; clipboard-write; encrypted-media; gyroscope; picture-in-picture" allowfullscreen="" style="border-radius: 10px; box-shadow: rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.1) 0px 4px 20px;"></iframe></div></div><div class="row gy-4 align-items-center features-item aos-init aos-animate" data-aos="fade-up" data-aos-delay="200"><div class="col-lg-5 d-flex justify-content-center flex-column"><h3>EarlyScreen: Predicting Neural Activation &amp; Psychopathology in Preschool Children</h3><p>Emotion dysregulation in early childhood is associated with a higher risk of psychopathological conditions, such as ADHD and mood and anxiety disorders. 
        EarlyScreen is a multi-scale instance fusion framework trained on behavioral markers during emotion regulation to predict neural activation and classify psychopathological risk.</p><ul><li><i class="bi bi-check"></i> <span>Predicts activation levels in the prefrontal cortex with an ROC-AUC of 0.85.</span></li><li><i class="bi bi-check"></i> <span>Classifies clinical and non-clinical subjects based on psychopathological risk with an ROC-AUC of 0.80.</span></li><li><i class="bi bi-check"></i> <span>Supports emotion regulation-related screening for psychopathological disorders in young children.</span></li></ul><a href="https://dl.acm.org/doi/10.1145/3534583" class="btn btn-get-started align-self-start" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Learn More</a></div><div class="col-lg-7 d-flex align-items-center justify-content-center"><iframe width="100%" height="400" src="https://www.youtube.com/embed/J74PHs3m2xM" title="EarlyScreen: Predicting Neural Activation &amp; Psychopathology in Preschool Children" frameborder="0" allow="accelerometer; autoplay; clipboard-write; encrypted-media; gyroscope; picture-in-picture" allowfullscreen="" style="border-radius: 10px; box-shadow: rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.1) 0px 4px 20px;"></iframe></div></div><div class="row gy-4 align-items-center features-item flex-row-reverse aos-init aos-animate" data-aos="fade-up" data-aos-delay="300"><div class="col-lg-5 d-flex justify-content-center flex-column"><h3>OpiTrack: A Wearable-based Clinical Opioid Use Tracker with Temporal Convolutional Attention Networks</h3><p>OpiTrack leverages physiological signal data from E4 wristwatches to predict intravenous opioid administrations in clinical settings using a temporal convolutional attention network.</p><ul><li><i class="bi bi-check"></i> <span>Detects IV opioid administrations using a time window.</span></li><li><i class="bi bi-check"></i> <span>Predicts the moment of administration with high precision.</span></li><li><i class="bi bi-check"></i> <span>Developed using channel-temporal attention TCN architecture.</span></li></ul><a href="https://doi.org/10.1145/3478107" class="btn btn-get-started align-self-start" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Learn More</a></div><div class="col-lg-7 d-flex align-items-center justify-content-center"><iframe width="100%" height="400" src="https://www.youtube.com/embed/zo2sz6DhK84" title="OpiTrack: A Wearable-based Clinical Opioid Use Tracker with Temporal Convolutional Attention Networks" frameborder="0" allow="accelerometer; autoplay; clipboard-write; encrypted-media; gyroscope; picture-in-picture" allowfullscreen="" style="border-radius: 10px; box-shadow: rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.1) 0px 4px 20px;"></iframe></div></div><div class="row gy-4 align-items-center features-item aos-init aos-animate" data-aos="fade-up" data-aos-delay="400"><div class="col-lg-5 d-flex justify-content-center flex-column"><h3>NeRF-enabled Analysis-Through-Synthesis for ISAR Imaging of Small Everyday Objects with Sparse and Noisy UWB Radar Data</h3><p>This study proposes a novel Analysis-through-Synthesis (ATS) framework enabled by Neural Radiance Fields (NeRF) for high-resolution coherent ISAR imaging of small objects using sparse and noisy Ultra-Wideband (UWB) radar data with an inexpensive and portable setup.</p><ul><li><i class="bi bi-check"></i> <span>Generates ISAR images of complex scenes in Non-Line-of-Sight (NLOS) scenarios.</span></li><li><i class="bi bi-check"></i> <span>Outperforms traditional ISAR reconstruction methods using sparse UWB radar scans.</span></li><li><i class="bi bi-check"></i> <span>Enables practical, cost-effective ISAR imaging of small everyday objects.</span></li></ul><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.10085" class="btn btn-get-started align-self-start" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Learn More</a></div><div class="col-lg-7 d-flex align-items-center justify-content-center"><iframe width="100%" height="400" src="https://www.youtube.com/embed/n6-XmvO5NQQ" title="NeRF-enabled Analysis-Through-Synthesis for ISAR Imaging of Small Everyday Objects with Sparse and Noisy UWB Radar Data" frameborder="0" allow="accelerometer; autoplay; clipboard-write; encrypted-media; gyroscope; picture-in-picture" allowfullscreen="" style="border-radius: 10px; box-shadow: rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.1) 0px 4px 20px;"></iframe></div></div></div></section></section>

            function openMailApp() {
                var name = document.querySelector('input[name="name"]').value;
                var email = document.querySelector('input[name="email"]').value;
                var subject = document.querySelector('input[name="subject"]').value;
                var message = document.querySelector('textarea[name="message"]').value;
        
                // Construct mailto link with pre-filled subject and body
                var mailtoLink = 'mailto:trahman@ucsd.edu' +
                                 '?subject=' + encodeURIComponent(subject) +
                                 '&body=' + "Dear Dr.Rahman, %0A%0A" + encodeURIComponent(message) + "%0A%0ABest regards,%0A" + encodeURIComponent(name);
                
                document.querySelector('.loading').style.display = 'block';
        
                // Open mail client with pre-filled details
                window.location.href = mailtoLink;

                // Hide loading animation and show sent message after 0.5 seconds (to simulate form submission)
                setTimeout(function() {
                    document.querySelector('.loading').style.display = 'none';
                    document.querySelector('.sent-message').style.display = 'block';
                }, 500);
            }
        </script>
